core_obligations: Reduce the sheaf condition: by the criterion for the fpqc topology on the category of schemes over S it suffices to check Zariski coverings and faithfully flat morphisms of affine schemes; the author also points to the corresponding statement in the Descent chapter (proof lines 1344-1350).
Zariski case: for an open immersion i : U -> S one has Gamma(U, i^*F) = F(U), so the sheaf property in the Zariski case is ordinary scheme theory (proof lines 1350-1353).

Affine faithfully flat case: for Spec(B) -> Spec(A) with A -> B faithfully flat and F|Spec(A) = M-tilde, the sheaf condition for F^a is the exactness of 0 -> M -> B tensor_A M -> B tensor_A B tensor_A M, i.e. the statement M = H^0((B/A)_bullet tensor_A M), which is exactly the descent lemma for modules (proof lines 1355-1365).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to two kinds of coverings by the standard criterion for the fpqc topology (proof lines 1347-1350).
Settle the Zariski case by the identification of sections of a pullback along an open immersion (proof lines 1351-1353).
Settle the affine faithfully flat case by the exactness of the Amitsur complex for a faithfully flat ring map, which is the quoted descent lemma (proof lines 1355-1365).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for a quasi-coherent sheaf F on S the presheaf F^a : (T -> S) -> Gamma(T, f^*F) on the category of schemes over S is an O-module satisfying the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology (statement lines 1333-1341). The work is to translate a sheaf-theoretic condition into algebra: after reducing to Zariski coverings and faithfully flat affine morphisms, the affine case is exactly the exactness of 0 -> M -> B tensor_A M -> B tensor_A B tensor_A M for a faithfully flat A -> B, which is the descent lemma for modules, and the Zariski case collapses because pullback along an open immersion has the same sections (proof lines 1350-1365). The reduction step and the identification of the Amitsur complex with the sheaf condition are what make the proposition non-immediate. The claim is H2.
